Not a puzzle game so much as it is a relaxing game. You don't get anything that requires any thought until you're pretty something like forty levels into it, and then it's over; before that, the game's just introducing mechanics in a bunch of different contexts. And even when you do get to some tougher stuff, the difficulty mostly stays low; you just get a few that challenge you, here and there.

In spite of all that, I liked it. The simplicity of most levels means you never lose your sense of flow, and it ends up being a nice experience. I've played a bit of Maciej Targoni's oeuvre by now, and that seems to be his niche.

This game contains 82 levels (puzzles). For me, the first 36 levels weren't really puzzles; I found them very simple to “solve”. Starting with level 37, when rotatable tiles appear, it gets more interesting, and some of the later puzzles are tricky. I finished the entire thing in about an hour, and for $2.99 I'm satisfied with what I got.
